title: Good Faith Estimates for Self-Pay Laboratory Test Orders
content:
## Who receives an estimate

A good faith estimate on Laboratory Test Orders is issued only for an order billed self-pay, or for a patient with no active coverage on file. Insured patients billing their plan receive no good faith estimate; their cost is determined by the plan's adjudication.

| Order billed | Active coverage on file | Good faith estimate |
|---|---|---|
| Self-pay | Either | Issued |
| Insurance | None active | Issued |
| Insurance | Yes | Not issued; the plan's adjudication determines the cost |

## When it is issued

An estimate is issued within the class's on-request period, in business days, after the patient's request. Alternatively, it is issued within the class's scheduled-collection period, in business days, once a self-pay collection is booked at least three business days ahead. Business days are Monday to Friday, excluding federal holidays.

## How long it applies

An estimate applies to a collection made within the class's estimate validity period, in calendar days from the estimate date. The estimate date is day 0 and the last day is included.

| Collection made on | Estimate applies |
|---|---|
| The estimate date plus the validity period | Yes |
| The following day | No; the estimate has lapsed |

## Retired clauses

> *No longer in force.* The former clause read: "when an add-on test is accepted on a self-pay order, or the estimate has lapsed before collection, a new estimate replaces the old one on every order of the encounter."

> *No longer in force.* The former clause read: "The amount follows the requisition-encounter rule."

Both clauses are no longer in force: they have been superseded by the current basis for good faith estimates. The rules above on who receives an estimate, when it is issued and how long it applies remain in force.
